title: ～から～にかけて — from ～ through ～
summary: Shows a broad span of time or space by roughly giving its start and end. It is used when the boundaries are not sharp. It follows nouns.

patterns.gloss: N1 から N2 にかけて

body.p: 'A から B にかけて' means the state continues or happens somewhere across the span from A to B. It is common in weather forecasts and in descriptions of seasons and regions. The range is loose.
から～まで marks a clear start and end. から～にかけて gives a rough span, so it does not suit precise times such as 'a meeting from nine to ten.'

examples.ja: 夜（よる）から朝（あさ）にかけて雨（あめ）が降（ふ）るでしょう。
examples.romaji: Yoru kara asa ni kakete ame ga furu deshō.
examples.tr: It will rain from night through morning.

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）の夕方（ゆうがた）から夜（よる）にかけて、風（かぜ）が強（つよ）くなるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kyō no yūgata kara yoru ni kakete, kaze ga tsuyoku naru deshō.
examples.tr: The wind will get stronger from this evening into the night.

examples.ja: この辺（あた）りは春（はる）から夏（なつ）にかけて、花（はな）がきれいに咲（さ）く。
examples.romaji: Kono atari wa haru kara natsu ni kakete, hana ga kirei ni saku.
examples.tr: Around here, flowers bloom beautifully from spring to summer.

pitfalls: Do not use it for exact times or periods. 九時から十時にかけて会議 sounds odd.
You need both から and にかけて; にかけて alone changes the meaning.
